properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/20/2021 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Covington Twp, Tioga county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/20/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 934016
Permit API: 117-20337
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Covington Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/20/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection on Seneca Resource's Covington Pad G (Pino Pad G) located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 10/20/2021 at 1035 hours. The weather was 63 degrees with clear skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of ~30 gallons of produced water to the pad surface that occurred on 10/7/2021. Complaint Tracking System ID #359859 is tied to this release. On 10/7/2021, Seneca Resource's contacted the DEP spill reporting hotline to report that ~30 gallons of produced water had released to the pad surface after a wash-out had occurred on the produced water flow-line. Produced water was discovered to have been released from the flow-line at a point where insulation was wrapped around the line. Upon removing the insulation, a small spray of produced water covered an area approximately 20ft by 5ft in area. The impacted area was then screened and excavated to remediate the release. All excavated material was placed into residual waste containers to await proper disposal. Samples were collected to ensure remediation efforts were efficient. While onsite today, the area was observed (photo #2) and pooled water had filled the excavated pit. Water within the pit was field measured at ~920us/cm today. Other pooled water and soils in the direct surrounding area were all field measured below 1.0mS/cm. I spoke with a Seneca representative while onsite who explained that they are awaiting confirmatory sample results before backfilling occurs. I agreed with the plan and contacted Andy Woodward with Seneca Resources to confirm. Upon confirmatory sample results showing normal ranges, the area will be backfilled with clean fill. Based on the release of ~30 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and the timely remediation conducted by Seneca, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-20337: 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) SWMA 301 CSL 402(b) I departed the site at 1130 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/11/2024 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/06/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8183523
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: On 4/11/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 56 degrees, overcast and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Justin Green and HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Justin described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. They were currently drilling the production section on the 76HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,228 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,544 feet. Justin accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board.Due to recent rainfall, water puddles were present on the pad surface. I sampled a channel of water along the east side of the north perimeter berm that had demonstrated in prior inspections as having elevated levels of conductivity. The water field tested at 2.36 mS conductance near where a white residue could be seen on the gravel. The water field tested at 2.13 near the pad outfall in the center of the north perimeter berm and field tested at 2.11 mS as the water was running down the outfall. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin field tested at 2.15mS conductance. Water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 0.869 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 0.88 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. I did witness emerging vegetation in the constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Standing water was present in the basins.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.3. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.4. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Ivory 1 well conducted on 1/12/2024. Arrived on location at 10:03. Violations were issued on 3/23/2022, 9/22/2022, and 5/2/2023 site inspections for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. This 1/12/2024 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack, meter, and electric boxes remain on site. Much of the equipment has been dismantled. Wellhead is no longer tied inline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Wellhead and much of the equipment is overgrown with trees/brush. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/20/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. Annual Production Reports have been submitted with 0 production shown for at least the last five years. All of the above violations remain outstanding.

Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued for the accelerated erosion and lack of maintenance of the access road. Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "Morgan 073" Marcellus well site.Harry Lammy (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday October 30, 2024 to report an estimated 20 gallon produced liquid release to the south end of the pad surface that day.Murray Kush (Repsol, Company Man) showed me where the produced liquid spill occurred when a vac truck overfilled on the south end of the pad surface near the gray cylindrical tanks. Gas Field Services removed the impacted pad material with guidance from Resource Management and placed it in an open top dumpster within 24 hours of the release. Soil in the remediated area has electrical conductivity of 0.02 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test meter. I did not observe any residual impacts from the spill. Precision Drilling 572 drilled the new wells into the Marcellus Shale in February-April 2024, adding to the existing 4 Marcellus wells at this site. Pro Frac hydraulically fractured the 4 new Marcellus wells here August 29-September 16, 2024. Repsol started flowing back liquid from the 4 new Marcellus wells on October 12, 2024 into the 37 tanks on the south end of the pad. They expect to finish flowback operations in about 1 week. Vegetation, rock, and erosion blanket stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Repsol constructed a new bioretention basin on the south end of the site, and removed the old basin.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist soil in 3 separate areas on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.02-0.12 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 63FJLP

The contractor then mobilized a second load of cement and placed an additional 140-sack Type I cement plug (28-barrel slurry) from 2,070 feet to 1,332 feet. JWS will return to tag and verify the top of cement on the following day.

Violation ID: 887752
Permit API: 083-54017
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-29
Comments: The operator contacted Brian Ayers to report multiple spills at the Collins Pine 22 well site the morning of 6/29/2020. This inspection was performed as a complaint inspection to CID #350759. The operator was intending to perform an injection test on this well for a proposed injection well permit. They had a 500 barrel laydown tank on location that was filled with brine over the course of several days prior to the test. The operator noted on arriving at the site 6/29 that the site was wet, and then was able to see that the tank was actively leaking brine. They were able to contact a vac truck operator who sent trucks to empty the tank. A mini excavator was used to dig a small trench on the north side of the site. In the interim, the operator hooked a hose from the tank to drain into the well in order to reduce the level of the tank. The packer in the well failed, which allowed oil to be displaced and flow out the backside of the packer string and onto the ground. The operator noticed the discharge and immediately shut the well in and ceased flowing water. They had a mini excavator on site and dug another interceptor trench in the access road to cut off oil from flowing further down gradient toward Route 6. 1-2 barrels of oil was estimated to have been released from this well. At the time of this inspection, the operator had determined that 3" of water had drained from the full tank prior to discovery of the leak, which occurred at approximately 10 am. Further leaking occurred during the time between discovery and the emptying of the tank at approximately 2 PM. The total loss of brine is estimated to be between 5 and 10 barrels. Various areas surrounding the tank were tested with a soil EC meter, which read between 15 mS and >20 mS. Oil was all contained within the trench or puddles on the location, with no threat of further contamination. The operator intends to have a rolloff container on site this evening and begin to scrape up the contaminated soil on site, starting with the area contaminated with crude oil. A vac truck will be on site should extra encountered.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "DCNR 587 017" Marcellus well site.Megan DePue (Repsol, Remediation and Reclamation) called the DEP today to report that Pete Lorson (Repsol, Facilities) discovered an estimated 10 gallons of drilling mud leaked thru liner containment onto the gravel pad surface. She emailed that the mud used on these wells was water based for the top portion, and diesel based for the deeper section. I spoke with Lorson on site who explained the following: Repsol finished drilling the 7 new Marcellus wells at this site about 2 weeks ago. Today they removed some of the matting to check for subsidence where pipes attached to the Marcellus wells are buried, and discovered some drilling mud leaked thru breaches in the liner.When I arrived on site at about 1415 hrs they were mostly done with the excavation of the impacted pad material. They filled one dumpster with the pad material, and were waiting on another dumpster to dispose of the remaining material that was excavated into a pile. I used a MiniRae 3000 Photo Ionization Detector with a 10.6 eV lamp to screen the excavated area. It returned a 0.0 ppm reading, indicating absence of volatile substances in the material. I also screened the top of a Marcellus well cellar, which returned a 0.4 ppm reading. I used a Hanna Groline soil probe and got 0.23-0.39 mS/cm electrical conductivity readings in the excavated area.Air temp 78FJLP

Violation ID: 851859
Permit API: 131-20585
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-05-29
Comments: I arrived at the site at 10:34 in response to a reported spill incident of an unknown volume of a fluid substance spilled to the pad surface, and into stormwater in a site perimeter ditch. The weather conditions are partly cloudy skies, breezy, warm and humid, with temperatures in the low to mid 70's. Representing the Department during the inspection in addition to myself include Ken Kennedy, Eric Miller, Cassidy Moyer and Eric Rooney. Marvin Schellie, consultant of BKV, is the company man at the site. Representing BKV is Tom Weller, Matt Knight and Dale Bennett. Representing the BKV consultant Apex Environmental is Shelly Bowen, and Jamie Moran. Kevin Brady of Whitetail Environmental, a BKV consultant, is also at the site. The current drilling depth on the Reynolds 2H well is (3,096) feet. Air drilling is in progress. The intermediate casing was cemented on 5/27/19 according to Mr. Schellie. Mr. Weller explained that inadvertently, a bypass valve for an overflow line was left open on the Iron Horse shale gas separator. Following waiting on cement (WOC), displacement fluid was being unloaded from the intermediate casing, and the existing separator tank was half full. When changed over and pressuring up to resume air drilling, air and some remaining displacement fluid was inadvertently discharged across the open top tank under pressure, and overflowed the tank and containment. Mr. Weller estimated that less than (1) barrel (42) gallons, was released off containment. Mr. Weller explained that the displaced water was recycled from previous air drilling operations, which may include the use of various lube products, and air foaming and defoaming products. Mr. Brady provided the Department with Safety Data Sheets (SDS) of the products. The SDS indicates the chemical name for the lube product is ECO Drill 100, with biodegradable drill oil listed as a synonym. The SDS indicates the foaming product is FoamFresh, with Eco-Friendly Foamer listed as a synonym. Mr. Brady also provided the Department with photos of the source of the fluid spilled out of the container, the ditch which is labeled stormwater channel, and a map of the site. The container is located on secondary containment in the area on the pad surface termed the backyard by BKV. This particular area is located adjacent to the drilling rig and site perimeter berm. Mr. Brady informed the Department that he recorded specific conductance (conductivity) of (4) millisiemens/cm in water in the stormwater channel on 5/28/19 at 15:35, (145) parts per million in chlorides on a Hach test strip on 5/28/19 at 15:35, and a sump was constructed in the channel as a result of the elevated readings. He further stated that an on-site vacuum truck was immediately deployed to the area where the spill occurred, and an additional vacuum truck was dispatched to remove impacted stormwater in the channel. Apex informed the Department they screened the impacted area on the ground surface with a photoionization detector (PID) meter for the potential presence of volatile organic compounds at 8:24 AM today, 5/29/19, and screened the water in the channel for conductivity at 8:40 AM today, 5/29/19. Apex indicated they excavated small holes in (3) locations on the berm where the impact occurred, to obtain PID readings. The reading at the first location was (1.9) ppm; the second location was (1.6) ppm, and the third location was 1.5 ppm. The PID meter read (0) parts per million on containment near the tank as part of the release. Conductivity was (306) microsiemens/cm. I used a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test meter, and an Oakton PCTS 50 meter to record conductivity of water in the channel. During the inspection, the Department and Apex collected samples of stormwater in the channel in (3) separate locations. The Department also collected a sample of fluid in the container associated with the spill. See photos. The Department left the site at 13:28.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp

Inspection Date: 1/24/2023
Comments: On 1/23/23 CHK reported a release of 42 gallons of produced water onto the pad surface. The release occurred around 11:00 on 1/23/23 when a produced water tank dump valve stuck open. It was estimated that the affected area was about 20' x 20'. The produced water tank was located on the northern side of the pad near the access road. At the time of inspection, the impacted area was revised to approximately 60' x 70' oriented north-south by east-west. The excavated area was approximately 10" - 12" deep. The excavation was being guided by conductivity measurements performed by Creston. The produced water tank will need to be moved in order to excavate the impacted area near the base and under the tank. The full depth of the excavation can not be determined until the tank is cleaned and moved, likely tomorrow 1/25/23.Conductivity measurements were taken around the the perimeter of the excavation. The measurements ranged from 0.02 to 0.390 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). A roadside ditch running along the access road and leading to an infiltration basin below the produced water tank was also inspected and screened. The site was snow-covered and no visual evidence of runoff was noted. Soil conductivity readings were below 0.20 mS/cm.The result of the inspection is Violations Noted and Act 2 remediation will be pursued.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-07-09
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report of elevated conductivity fluid discovered on the pad on 7/7/20. Dillon Otten reported on 7/7/20 that fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) between 11-12 mS/cm was discovered during excavation adjacent to the 2H well head. An estimated release volume was provided of 42 gallons. Four wells were recently fraced and completed on this pad. These wells were being plumbed into the production equipment on the pad at the time of this inspection. Four existing wells are present on the pad and in production. Upon arriving on location, I observed the trench adjacent to the 2H well head. A sump was present close to the well head and a small puddle was present within the sump. No fluid was observed flowing into or out of the sump. The other areas in the trench were dry. No staining or puddles were present on the pad surface. The fluid in the sump had an EC of 15.06 mS/cm. Due to the reported spill volume of 42 gallons, Act 2 remediation is required by 78a.66. The Department recommends investigating the source of the elevated conductivity fluid. Violations noted.

Violation ID: 976073
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/16/2022
Comments: On 11/16/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. This inspection is in response to Complaint Id 368309 for one barrel of brine water spilled outside of secondary containment from a frac tank on the site.Prior to my arrival, Chesapeake's Danielle Schaad informed me that the frac tank would be to the right when arriving on site and was stationed in secondary containment by itself. She said that the location of the leak in the frac tank and in the secondary containment was unknown but high conductance water was discovered outside of secondary containment on the pad surface. She said that the fluid was brine water from the produced water tank. She reported that the tank and secondary containment had been emptied and the puddle vacuumed up. She said that the tank was being removed from location and that Cresson Environmental would be onsite on 11/17/2022. It was 40 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy snowfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours and was melting with the pad being mostly clear of snow. A skid steer and a vac truck had just arrived on location and were setting up next to a frac tank in the northeast corner of the site. The frac tank was still connected to the 1HC gas well GPU. A crew was working on disconnecting it from the GPU. A vac box was located south of the frac tank. I field tested various water puddles in close proximity to the frac tank for conductance using an Oakton PCTS 50 with an upper limit of 20.0 mS with the following results: 40'x 40' water puddle on the south west corner of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 0.77 mS.5' x 8' water puddle outside the southeast corner of the vac box field tested at 14.43 mS.20' x 20' water puddle southeast of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.15 x 30' water puddle east of the frac tank secondary containment was over 20.0 mS.6' x 20' water puddle northeast of the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 3.53 mS.12' x 40' water puddle on the east edge of the site above the recently excavated fill slope field tested at 2.33 mS.Water below the rocked section of the fill slope field tested at 1.20 mS. Water in the south end of infiltration area 1 field tested at 1.40 mS.Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at 0.8 mS or less.There were ten wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. A rainbow sheen was witnessed in the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. There were six frac tanks and one gas buster staged in secondary containment on the west side of location. While on site the frac tank with the suspected leak and the secondary containment were removed from location. Water puddles adjacent to the frac tank location were vacuumed up. Joe Button discussed that an excavator will be brought to location along with Creston Environmental to conduct cleanup operations at 0800 hrs on 11/17/2022. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 56[a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b)The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c)The department also recommends removing the water from and cleaning the well cellars noted for having sheens; the Hopson 101HC, 22HC, 4HC and 5H well cellars.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3406647 for high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities with an unknown volume impacting the pad surface.I left the site at 1400 hours.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8276970
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/09/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/09/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 959022
Permit API: 081-21884
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/09/2022
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water occurred which then overflowed secondary containment during completion operations on Pad B. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. According to Mr. Hall, a hose failed which was hooked up to a booster pump that was being used for coiled tubing operations at the time of the release. After the secondary containment overflowed, the produced water flowed toward the stormwater channel along the pad edge. Mr. Hall said that he would have a sump dug in the stormwater channel at the pad edge to attempt to recover as much of the release as possible. Due to the amount of equipment on the pad and the waterlines and electrical cables along the side of the pad, Hall said that little excavation would be possible until completion operations were finished. He said that completions may be done as soon as the middle of July. He also said that Creston Environmental was en route to conduct screening of the site. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed hose and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted.

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/27/2021
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.

Permit API: 131-20529
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/22/2024
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build-Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess recent remedial work of Perf. and Squeeze Ops. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20"x 13 3/8") annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20" x13 3/8") annulus is capped and set up for venting via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve (Sentry replaced with bull plug for testing). Both wells remained in production through the SPBUT period. All annuli of each well have been shut in for testing. The (20"x13") annulus was shut in for 72hrs., the (13"x9") annuli were shut in for 48hrs. and the (9"x5") annuli were shut in for 24hrs. resulting in SPBUTs. - Prior to shutting in the wells on (2/19/24) gas screenings and flow checks were performed w/ Alicat meter (20 slpm) w/ 0.250 orifice on all well annuli except the open top (20x13) annulus of the 4H. - Pre-shut in results: - WYO 4H: - (20x13): open top annulus - (13x9): 30,760 ppm gas; 0.001 slpm flow = 0.05 Cu. ft./d - (9x5): 88% gas; 6.975 slpm flow = 354.7 Cu. ft./d - WYO 2H: - (20x13): 65% gas; 0.012 slpm flow = 0.6 Cu. ft./d - (13x9): 10% gas; 0.002 slpm flow = 0.10 Cu. ft./d - (9x5): 85% gas; 1.525 slpm flow = 77.6 Cu. ft./d - Starting at approx. 12:00 today (2/22/24) ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. (2/22/24). - Ending pressures, gas checks are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 0 psi.; 30,760 ppm gas; No Sample taken - (9x5): 190 psi.; 88% gas; No Sample taken - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 10 psi.; 65% gas; No Sample taken * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 0 psi.; 10% gas; No Sample taken - (9x5); 99 psi.; 85% gas; No Sample taken - All annuli were returned to venting by 12:25
